chapters.1.summary: Solomon is established as king, and God is with him. He leads the assembly to Gibeon, where the tent of meeting stands. He offers a thousand burnt offerings on the bronze altar. That night God tells him to ask for whatever he wants. Solomon asks for wisdom and knowledge to lead the people. God gives him that, with riches and honor besides. Solomon gathers chariots and horsemen. He buys horses from Egypt and makes silver common in Jerusalem.
chapters.1.lds: Why does Solomon ask for wisdom before asking for wealth?
chapters.2.summary: Solomon decides to build a house for the LORD’s name and a palace. He writes to Huram king of Tyre for cedar and a master craftsman. He admits that even the highest heaven cannot contain God. He offers wheat, barley, wine, and oil for Tyre’s woodcutters. Huram praises the LORD and sends a craftsman of mixed descent. The logs will come by sea to Joppa. Solomon counts the foreigners living in Israel. He makes them carriers, stonecutters, and overseers.
chapters.2.lds: Whose skills and labor make the temple possible?
chapters.3.summary: Solomon begins to build the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. The site is Mount Moriah, at the threshing floor of Ornan. He starts in the fourth year of his reign. The main room is overlaid with fine gold and set with precious stones. The inner room holds two great cherubim whose wings span the width. A veil of blue, purple, and crimson hangs before it. Two tall pillars stand in front of the house. They are named Jachin and Boaz.
chapters.3.lds: The Seminary manual connects Moriah with sacred space and temple worship. What two names does verse 1 give the site?
chapters.4.summary: Solomon makes a bronze altar twenty cubits square. He makes the great basin called the sea, resting on twelve oxen. He makes ten smaller basins and ten gold lampstands. He makes ten tables and a hundred gold bowls. He builds a court for the priests and a great outer court. Huram finishes the pots, shovels, pillars, and stands. The bronze is too much to weigh. The gold altar, tables, lamps, and doors complete the furnishings.
chapters.4.lds: What different tasks do the temple’s vessels serve?
chapters.5.summary: The temple is finished, and Solomon brings in David’s dedicated treasures. The elders gather in Jerusalem at the feast. Levites carry the ark, and the king offers more sacrifices than can be counted. The priests set the ark under the cherubim’s wings. Only the two stone tablets are in it. Singers in fine linen stand with a hundred twenty priests blowing trumpets. They praise the LORD together, for his kindness lasts forever. A cloud fills the house, and the priests cannot stand to serve.
chapters.5.lds: The Seminary manual compares dedication experiences with later LDS temple worship. What happens when the singers and trumpeters sound “as one” (verse 13)?
chapters.6.summary: Solomon blesses the people and recalls the promise to David. He kneels on a bronze platform and spreads his hands. He says heaven cannot contain God, much less this house. He asks God to hear prayers made toward this place. He names sin, defeat, drought, famine, and sickness. He prays for the foreigner who comes from far away. He prays for Israel in battle and in exile. He asks God to arise and come to his resting place.
chapters.6.lds: Why does Solomon include foreigners in his prayer?
chapters.7.summary: When Solomon finishes praying, fire from heaven burns up the offerings. The LORD’s glory fills the house, and the people bow to the ground. The king and people offer thousands of animals. They keep the feast for seven days and the dedication for seven more. The LORD appears to Solomon at night. He promises to hear and heal the land when his people humble themselves and pray. If they turn to other gods, he will uproot them. The house will become a warning to all who pass.
chapters.7.lds: The Seminary manual studies the dedication as an account of divine acceptance. What condition does verse 19 set?
chapters.8.summary: Solomon spends twenty years building the temple and his palace. He rebuilds towns and settles Israelites in them. He fortifies cities for stores, chariots, and horsemen. The remaining Canaanite peoples are made forced laborers. He moves Pharaoh’s daughter out of David’s city. He offers sacrifices on the days and feasts that Moses commanded. He sets the priests, Levites, and gatekeepers in the order David gave. His ships sail with Huram’s sailors and bring gold from Ophir.
chapters.8.lds: How do workers and sailors support Solomon’s kingdom?
chapters.9.summary: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions. He answers all of them. She sees his house, his table, his servants, and his offerings. She says the report did not tell half of his wisdom. She blesses God, who set him on God’s throne to do justice. She gives gold, spices, and precious stones and returns home. Solomon’s gold, ivory throne, and trading ships are described. He rules forty years and dies.
chapters.9.lds: What does the queen ask about Solomon’s wisdom and God’s care for Israel?
chapters.10.summary: Rehoboam goes to Shechem, where all Israel has come to make him king. Jeroboam and the people ask him to lighten his father’s heavy yoke. He asks for three days. The old men who served Solomon advise kindness. He rejects their advice and asks the young men he grew up with. They tell him to promise a heavier yoke. He answers the people harshly. Israel rejects David’s house, and only Judah’s towns stay with him.
chapters.10.lds: Why does Rehoboam reject the advice to ease the people’s burden?
chapters.11.summary: Rehoboam gathers one hundred eighty thousand soldiers to win back Israel. The prophet Shemaiah brings the LORD’s word against the war. The army listens and goes home. Rehoboam fortifies fifteen cities in Judah and Benjamin. Priests and Levites leave their lands in the north and come to Jerusalem. Jeroboam had removed them and made his own priests. Others who seek the LORD follow them. For three years they strengthen Rehoboam, and his family grows large.
chapters.11.lds: Why do priests and Levites leave the northern kingdom?
chapters.12.summary: When Rehoboam’s rule is strong, he and all Israel abandon the LORD’s law. In his fifth year Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem. Shemaiah says they left the LORD, so he has left them to Shishak. The king and the leaders humble themselves and say the LORD is right. The LORD grants some rescue and does not destroy them. Shishak takes the treasures of the temple and palace. Rehoboam replaces Solomon’s gold shields with bronze. He rules seventeen years in all.
chapters.12.lds: How does Rehoboam respond when Shemaiah explains Judah’s defeat?
chapters.13.summary: Abijah king of Judah goes to war against Jeroboam. Judah’s army is half the size of Israel’s. Abijah stands on a hill and speaks to the northern army. He says God gave the kingdom to David’s sons. He says the north has golden calves and has driven out the LORD’s priests. Jeroboam sets an ambush behind Judah. Judah cries to the LORD, and the priests blow the trumpets. God defeats Israel, and Abijah takes Bethel and other towns.
chapters.13.lds: What reasons does Abijah give for Judah’s trust in God?
chapters.14.summary: Asa does what is good and right. He removes foreign altars and tells Judah to seek the LORD. The land has ten years of peace. He builds walled cities and trains a large army. Zerah the Cushite comes against him with a far greater force. Asa prays that the LORD helps the weak as easily as the strong. The LORD strikes the Cushites, and they flee. Judah carries home much plunder, with sheep and camels.
chapters.14.lds: Come, Follow Me invites study of Asa’s trust during danger. On whom does Asa say Judah relies (verse 11)?
chapters.15.summary: God’s Spirit comes on Azariah, who meets Asa after the victory. He says the LORD is with them while they are with him. Israel once lived long without a teaching priest or law. Asa takes courage and removes idols from the land. He repairs the LORD’s altar. Many come to him from the northern tribes. The people swear a covenant with shouting and trumpets and great joy. Asa even removes his grandmother from her position for her idol.
chapters.15.lds: Come, Follow Me studies perseverance and trust through Asa’s reforms. What does Asa do after hearing the prophet (verse 8)?
chapters.16.summary: Baasha king of Israel fortifies Ramah to shut Judah in. Asa sends temple and palace treasure to the king of Syria. Syria attacks Israel’s northern towns, and Baasha stops building. The seer Hanani tells Asa he relied on Syria and not on the LORD. He reminds him of the victory over the Cushites. From now on Asa will have wars. Asa puts the seer in prison and mistreats some of the people. Late in life his feet are diseased, and he seeks only physicians.
chapters.16.lds: Come, Follow Me compares where Asa places his trust at different times. How does Asa treat the seer in verse 10?
chapters.17.summary: Jehoshaphat becomes king and strengthens Judah against Israel. He follows the ways of David and does not seek the Baals. The LORD establishes his kingdom, and he grows rich. In his third year he sends officials, Levites, and priests through Judah. They carry the book of the LORD’s law and teach in every city. Fear of the LORD falls on the nearby kingdoms. Philistines and Arabs bring him tribute. He builds forts and keeps a large army.
chapters.17.lds: How does Jehoshaphat use teachers to help his people learn God’s law?
chapters.18.summary: Jehoshaphat is rich and allied to Ahab by marriage. Ahab asks him to help retake Ramoth Gilead. Four hundred prophets promise victory. Jehoshaphat asks for another, and Micaiah is called. Micaiah sees Israel scattered and describes a lying spirit in the prophets’ mouths. Ahab jails him and goes to battle in disguise. The enemy surrounds Jehoshaphat, and he cries out and is spared. A random arrow strikes Ahab, and he dies at sunset.
chapters.18.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Micaiah’s truthful speech under pressure. What does the messenger ask of Micaiah in verse 12?
chapters.19.summary: Jehoshaphat returns safely, and the seer Jehu rebukes him for helping the wicked. Yet some good is found in him. The king travels among the people and brings them back to the LORD. He appoints judges in every fortified city. He tells them they judge for the LORD, not for man. In Jerusalem he sets up a court of Levites, priests, and family heads. The chief priest leads in the LORD’s matters. A leader of Judah handles the king’s matters.
chapters.19.lds: The Seminary manual connects correction with faithful service. What three things does verse 7 say are not found with the LORD?
chapters.20.summary: A great army from Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir comes against Judah. Jehoshaphat is afraid and calls a fast. All Judah gathers with wives and children. The king prays and admits they have no strength and no plan. The Spirit comes on Jahaziel, a Levite, who says the battle is God’s. Next morning singers march ahead of the army giving thanks. The enemy armies turn on one another. Judah gathers plunder for three days and blesses the LORD.
chapters.20.lds: Come, Follow Me studies prayer, trust, and prophetic encouragement. What does the king admit in verse 12?
chapters.21.summary: Jehoshaphat gives his sons gifts and cities and leaves the kingdom to Jehoram. Jehoram kills all his brothers and some of the princes. He marries Ahab’s daughter and follows Israel’s kings. The LORD spares David’s house because of the covenant. Edom and Libnah revolt. A letter from Elijah says Jehoram will die of disease. Raiders carry off his goods, wives, and sons. He dies in great pain, and no one regrets his death.
chapters.21.lds: How do Jehoram’s choices affect his brothers and the people he rules?
chapters.22.summary: Ahaziah becomes king of Judah. His mother Athaliah advises him to do evil. He joins Israel’s king in war and visits him at Jezreel. Jehu, who is destroying Ahab’s house, kills Ahaziah too. Athaliah then kills the royal children of Judah. Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, steals away the baby Joash. She hides him and his nurse in a bedroom. He stays hidden in God’s house for six years while Athaliah rules.
chapters.22.lds: What do Jehoshabeath and the nurse risk by hiding Joash?
chapters.23.summary: In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada makes a pact with the guard captains. They gather Levites and family heads from all Judah. Guards surround the young king with weapons from the temple. They crown Joash, hand him the testimony, and shout. Athaliah cries treason and is put to death outside the temple. Jehoiada makes a covenant with the people and the king. They tear down Baal’s temple. Gatekeepers are posted, and the city is quiet.
chapters.23.lds: Why does Jehoiada ask the people to promise loyalty to God when Joash becomes king?
chapters.24.summary: Joash does right all the days of the priest Jehoiada. He collects money in a chest and repairs the temple. Jehoiada dies very old and is buried among the kings. Then Judah’s princes persuade the king to leave the LORD’s house. Prophets warn them, and they do not listen. The Spirit comes on Zechariah, Jehoiada’s son, who rebukes the people. At the king’s command they stone him in the temple court. A small Syrian army defeats Judah, and Joash’s servants kill him.
chapters.24.lds: Why does Joash reject correction after Jehoiada’s death?
chapters.25.summary: Amaziah does right, but not with a whole heart. He hires a hundred thousand soldiers from Israel. A man of God says to send them home, and he obeys at a loss. He defeats Edom and then worships Edom’s gods. A prophet asks why he seeks gods that could not save their own people. The king threatens him into silence. Amaziah challenges Israel’s king and is badly beaten. Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and he later dies by conspiracy.
chapters.25.lds: How does Amaziah respond differently to his two warnings?
chapters.26.summary: Uzziah becomes king at sixteen and rules fifty-two years. He seeks God, and God gives him success. He defeats the Philistines, builds towers, digs cisterns, and loves farming. His army is large and has new war machines. When he is strong, his heart grows proud. He enters the temple to burn incense on the altar. Eighty priests confront him, and he becomes angry. A skin disease breaks out on his forehead, and he lives apart until he dies.
chapters.26.lds: Come, Follow Me studies humility and the limits on Uzziah’s incense offering. What do the priests tell the king in verse 18?
chapters.27.summary: Jotham becomes king at twenty-five and rules sixteen years. He does what is right, as his father Uzziah did. Unlike his father he does not enter the LORD’s temple. The people still act corruptly. He builds the upper gate of the temple and much on the city wall. He builds towns in the hills and forts in the forests. He defeats Ammon, which pays him tribute. He grows strong because he orders his ways before the LORD.
chapters.27.lds: What can a faithful leader do when others continue doing wrong?
chapters.28.summary: Ahaz makes idols and burns his children as offerings. Syria defeats him and takes captives. Israel’s king kills many of Judah’s soldiers and carries off women and children. The prophet Oded meets the army at Samaria. He says they have killed in rage and must not enslave their kin. Four leaders of Ephraim agree and stop the army. They clothe, feed, and carry the captives back to Jericho. Ahaz then seeks Assyria’s help, worships Syria’s gods, and shuts the temple.
chapters.28.lds: How do the northern leaders turn a victory into care for their captives?
chapters.29.summary: Hezekiah opens the temple doors in the first month of his reign. He tells the priests and Levites to make themselves and the house holy. They carry out the filth and finish in sixteen days. The king and the city leaders bring sin offerings for all Israel. Levites play the instruments David appointed, and the assembly bows. The people bring so many offerings that the priests need help. The Levites assist them. Hezekiah and the people rejoice at how quickly it was done.
chapters.29.lds: What work must the priests and Levites finish before temple worship can begin again?
chapters.30.summary: Hezekiah invites all Israel and Judah to keep the Passover in Jerusalem. It is held in the second month because the priests were not ready. Couriers carry letters north to Ephraim and Manasseh. Many laugh at them, but some humble themselves and come. Many who come have not made themselves clean. They eat anyway, and Hezekiah prays for their pardon. The LORD hears him and heals the people. The feast is so glad that they keep it seven more days.
chapters.30.lds: Come, Follow Me studies welcome, pardon, and peacemaking at Passover. For whom does Hezekiah pray in verses 18–19?
chapters.31.summary: After the feast the people break down the idols and altars across the land. Hezekiah sets the priests and Levites in their turns of service. He gives from his own herds for the regular offerings. He tells the people to give the priests’ and Levites’ share. They bring grain, wine, oil, and honey in heaps for four months. The chief priest says there is enough and plenty left over. Storerooms are prepared and keepers named. Men are chosen to hand out portions fairly in every town.
chapters.31.lds: How do careful storage and fair sharing support the temple workers’ families?
chapters.32.summary: Sennacherib of Assyria invades Judah and camps against its walled cities. Hezekiah stops the springs outside Jerusalem and repairs the wall. He makes weapons and tells the people that a greater one is with them. Assyrian officers shout insults at the people on the wall. Hezekiah and Isaiah cry to heaven. An angel destroys the Assyrian commanders, and Sennacherib goes home in shame. Later Hezekiah is sick, grows proud, and humbles himself. He also brings water down to the west side of David’s city.
chapters.32.lds: The Seminary manual highlights Hezekiah’s humility. What practical steps does Hezekiah take in verses 3–5?
chapters.33.summary: Manasseh rules fifty-five years and does great evil. He rebuilds the high places and sets an idol in God’s house. He burns his sons, uses sorcery, and ignores every warning. Assyrian commanders capture him and take him to Babylon in chains. In distress he humbles himself and prays. God hears and brings him back to Jerusalem. He removes the idols and repairs the LORD’s altar. His son Amon does evil, does not humble himself, and is killed.
chapters.33.lds: The Seminary manual highlights Manasseh’s prayer and humility. What changes Manasseh in verse 12?
chapters.34.summary: Josiah becomes king at eight. At sixteen he begins to seek God, and at twenty he clears away the idols. He carries the reform into the northern lands. In his eighteenth year he repairs the temple with honest workmen. While the money is brought out, the priest Hilkiah finds the book of the law. The king hears it and tears his clothes. His officials consult the prophetess Huldah, who confirms the coming disaster. Josiah gathers the people and renews the covenant.
chapters.34.lds: The Seminary manual connects scripture hearing with renewed covenants. To whom do the king’s men go in verse 22?
chapters.35.summary: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the proper day. He sets the priests and Levites in their places. He and his officials give thousands of animals for the people. No Passover like it had been kept since Samuel’s time. Later Pharaoh Neco marches north to fight at Carchemish. Josiah goes out against him. Neco says God sent him and warns Josiah to turn back. Josiah fights in disguise, is shot by archers, and dies in Jerusalem.
chapters.35.lds: Why does Josiah’s earlier faithfulness not settle what he should do in this battle?
chapters.36.summary: Judah’s last four kings rule under Egypt and then Babylon. Zedekiah will not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah. He breaks an oath he swore by God to Nebuchadnezzar. The LORD sends messengers again and again, out of pity for his people. They mock the prophets until there is no remedy. The Babylonians kill, burn the temple, and break down Jerusalem’s wall. The survivors become servants in Babylon for seventy years. Then Cyrus king of Persia permits the people to go up and rebuild.
chapters.36.lds: The Seminary manual reads captivity alongside God’s continuing care. What does Cyrus say God has told him to do (verse 23)?
